> **Pipeline step 05 — main-text / supplementary figures: model comparison.**
>
> **Purpose.** For each model set, a forest plot of ELPD (±SE) aligned row-for-row with a table
> of stacking weights and the optional covariates each model carries.
>
> **Inputs.** the ELPD comparison CSVs and criteria written by steps 01–03 (no full fits are
> loaded except the 14 TPS water-quality fits, for their `psis_loo` objects).
>
> **Outputs.** `output_figs/model_comparison_*` (PDF, TIFF, PNG).
>
> The salinity-included appendix versions (`sal_model_comparison_*`) are produced by
> `appendix_salinity_temperature_wateryear/A06_salinity_model_comparison_figures.R`, which
> re-uses the function chunks defined here.

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
For each of three model sets we build one composite figure:

* **Left** – a forest plot of the ELPD estimate for every fit (point = ELPD, bar = ±SE),
  models ordered best→worst (descending ELPD, best on top).
* **Right** – a table aligned row-for-row with the forest: a **stacking-weight** column
  followed by a grid of the **optional covariates**, with a filled box wherever a model
  includes that covariate.

The three sets and the predictive criterion behind their ELPD:

| folder                | criterion (ELPD)                                  |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `fits_tps_wq_Vfix/`   | PSIS-LOO with moment matching                     |
| `fits_edsm_Vfix/`     | grouped K-fold CV on `(1 | StationCode)`          |
| `fits_tps_fl_kfold/`  | grouped K-fold CV on `(1 | StationCode)`          |

Stacking weights are recomputed here **exactly** the way `Ensemble_cod_effect_plots_kfold.Rmd`
does (the single source of weights for the conditional-effect / forest figures): PSIS-LOO
sets go through `loo::loo_model_weights(method = "stacking")`; K-fold sets go through
`loo::stacking_weights()` on the matrix of pointwise `elpd_kfold`. Weights are computed over
the **full** model set, with no cutoff — so they match the CE and beta-forest plots.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(brms)
library(loo)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

OUT_DIR <- "output_figs"
if (!dir.exists(OUT_DIR)) dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE)

# ---- aesthetics (shared across the three figures so they compare cleanly) -----
FILL_COV    <- "#4C78A8"   # covariate-present cell fill
FILL_EMPTY  <- "white"     # covariate-absent cell fill
COL_GRID    <- "grey70"    # covariate grid lines (always visible)
COL_WBAR    <- "#4C78A8"   # stacking-weight bar
COL_POINT   <- "grey15"    # forest point / range

# ---- panel widths, in ABSOLUTE inches -----------------------------------------
# Panels are sized in inches (not relative units), so the forest plot and each
# covariate column are the SAME physical width in every figure regardless of how
# many covariate columns a survey has. The saved image width is then just the sum
# of the panels plus a fixed decoration allowance (y-axis, labels, margins).
# ADJUST FIGURE WIDTH HERE:
PANEL_FOREST_IN <- 2.9     # width of the forest (ELPD) panel
PANEL_WEIGHT_IN <- 0.55    # width of the stacking-weight column
PANEL_CELL_IN   <- 0.25    # width of ONE covariate column
PANEL_DECOR_IN  <- 1.30    # fixed non-panel width (forest y-axis + labels + margins)
```


## Stacking-weight helpers (mirror Ensemble_cod_effect_plots_kfold.Rmd)

```{r weight-helpers}
# Pointwise ELPD out of a stored predictive criterion (psis_loo or kfold).
.elpd_pointwise <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "psis_loo")) x$pointwise[, "elpd_loo"]
  else                          x$pointwise[, "elpd_kfold"]
}

# Stacking weights over a *named* list of criteria. If every element is a
# psis_loo object we use loo_model_weights() (the all-PSIS path in the ensemble
# notebook); otherwise we stack the pointwise elpd matrix directly. Result is a
# named numeric vector summing to 1 over the full set passed in.
stacking_weights_from_criteria <- function(crit_list, method = "stacking") {
  stopifnot(!is.null(names(crit_list)))
  all_psis <- all(vapply(crit_list, function(x) inherits(x, "psis_loo"), logical(1)))
  w <- if (all_psis) {
    loo::loo_model_weights(crit_list, method = method)
  } else {
    lpd_mat <- do.call(cbind, lapply(crit_list, .elpd_pointwise))
    if (method == "pseudobma") loo::pseudobma_weights(lpd_mat)
    else                       loo::stacking_weights(lpd_mat)
  }
  setNames(as.numeric(w), names(crit_list))
}
```


## Covariate bookkeeping

Each model's fixed-effects *core* (everything except the shared structural terms —
intercept, `s(water_year_day)` / `water_year_day_z`, `offset(log(Volume))` and the
`(1 | StationCode)` random intercept) is written out below, transcribed from the fitted
formulas (`*_output.txt`). `terms()` expands the `*` / `:` interactions to canonical term
labels, which are then mapped to display names. Encoding the formulas (rather than reading
the big fits) keeps this notebook fast and makes every model's covariate set auditable.

```{r covariate-defs}
# raw model term  ->  display label
COV_LABELS <- c(
  "out30_z"                              = "Outflow",
  "distance_along_channel_z"             = "Dist. along",
  "distance_m_z"                         = "Dist. offshore",
  "start_depth_z"                        = "Start depth",
  "habitat2020"                          = "Hydro",
  "Edge_Type"                            = "Edge type",
  "secchi_z"                             = "Secchi",
  "dox_z"                                = "DO",
  "chlorophyll_z"                        = "Chl-a",
  "ph_z"                                 = "pH",
  "out30_z:distance_m_z"                 = "Out × off",
  "distance_m_z:out30_z"                 = "Out × off",
  "out30_z:distance_along_channel_z"     = "Out × along",
  "distance_along_channel_z:out30_z"     = "Out × along"
)

# Left-to-right order of covariate columns in the table (subset to those present).
COV_ORDER <- c("Outflow", "Dist. along", "Dist. offshore", "Start depth",
               "Out × along", "Out × off", "Edge type",
               "Hydro", "Secchi", "DO", "Chl-a", "pH")

# Expand one core RHS string to display-labelled covariates ("" / "1" -> none).
core_to_covs <- function(core) {
  core <- trimws(core)
  if (!nzchar(core) || core == "1") return(character(0))
  raw <- attr(terms(as.formula(paste("~", core))), "term.labels")
  out <- COV_LABELS[raw]
  if (any(is.na(out))) stop("Unmapped term(s): ", paste(raw[is.na(out)], collapse = ", "))
  unname(out)
}

# fit name -> covariate-presence wide data frame (logical cols, ordered).
build_cov_matrix <- function(cores) {
  cov_sets <- lapply(cores, core_to_covs)
  present  <- intersect(COV_ORDER, unique(unlist(cov_sets)))
  mat <- vapply(cov_sets, function(cs) present %in% cs, logical(length(present)))
  df  <- as.data.frame(t(mat))
  names(df) <- present
  tibble::rownames_to_column(df, "fit")
}
```

## Read ELPD comparisons & compute stacking weights

```{r read-comparisons}
# Standardise a loo_compare CSV to: fit, elpd_diff, se_diff, elpd, se_elpd.
read_comparison <- function(path) {
  d <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  names(d)[1] <- "fit"
  if ("elpd_loo" %in% names(d)) {
    d$elpd <- d$elpd_loo;   d$se_elpd <- d$se_elpd_loo
  } else {
    d$elpd <- d$elpd_kfold; d$se_elpd <- d$se_elpd_kfold
  }
  tibble::as_tibble(d[, c("fit", "elpd_diff", "se_diff", "elpd", "se_elpd")])
}

```

```{r read-comparisons-data}
## --- EDSM: K-fold, weights from the pre-bundled criteria (no fits loaded) ----
edsm_nums  <- 0:21
edsm_fits  <- paste0("fit_edsm_", edsm_nums)
edsm_bundle <- readRDS("fits_edsm_Vfix/kfold5_station_criteria_bundle.rds")
edsm_crit   <- edsm_bundle[edsm_fits]                       # named, full set
w_edsm      <- stacking_weights_from_criteria(edsm_crit)
comp_edsm   <- read_comparison("fits_edsm_Vfix/fit_edsm_topmods_catch_kfold5_station_comparisons.csv")

## --- TPS fork length: K-fold, weights from the lightweight kfold sidecars ----

fl_fits   <- paste0("fit_tps_fl_", fl_nums)
fl_crit   <- setNames(
  lapply(fl_nums, function(i) readRDS(sprintf("fits_tps_fl_kfold/kfold69_tps_fl_%d.rds", i))),
  fl_fits
)
w_fl      <- stacking_weights_from_criteria(fl_crit)
comp_fl   <- read_comparison("fits_tps_fl_kfold/fit_tps_fl_kfold69_comparisons.csv")

## --- TPS water-quality: PSIS-LOO (moment matched), weights from fit$criteria$loo
## These are the only fits we load (small, ~28 MB each); needed for psis_loo objects.

wq_fits   <- paste0("fit_tps_wq", wq_nums)
wq_crit   <- setNames(
  lapply(wq_nums, function(i) readRDS(sprintf("fits_tps_wq_Vfix/fit_tps_wq%d.rds", i))$criteria$loo),
  wq_fits
)
w_wq      <- stacking_weights_from_criteria(wq_crit)        # all-PSIS -> loo_model_weights
comp_wq   <- read_comparison("fits_tps_wq_Vfix/fit_tps_wq1-13_catch_looic_comparisons.csv")

## --- TPS landscape: PSIS-LOO (moment matched), weights from the slim LOO sidecars
## (loo_tps<n>.rds are psis_loo objects with psis_object dropped; loo_model_weights
## uses their pointwise elpd_loo, matching the landscape notebook's stacking weights).
```

## Assemble one tidy table per model set

```{r assemble}
# Join comparison + weights + covariates; order rows best->worst by ELPD; make the
# shared y factor (model number) used by every panel so the rows line up.
assemble_group <- function(comp, weights, cores) {
  covs <- build_cov_matrix(cores)
  df <- comp %>%
    mutate(weight    = weights[fit],
           model_num = as.integer(str_extract(fit, "\\d+$"))) %>%
    left_join(covs, by = "fit") %>%
    arrange(elpd_diff) %>%                                  # worst -> best
    mutate(ylab = factor(model_num, levels = model_num))    # best ends up on top
  cov_cols <- intersect(COV_ORDER, names(df))
  list(df = df, cov_cols = cov_cols)
}

```

```{r assemble-data}
g_edsm <- assemble_group(comp_edsm, w_edsm, cores_edsm)
g_wq   <- assemble_group(comp_wq,   w_wq,   cores_tps_wq)
g_fl   <- assemble_group(comp_fl,   w_fl,   cores_tps_fl)
g_ls   <- assemble_group(comp_ls,   w_ls,   cores_tps_landscape)

# quick look at the EDSM table
g_edsm$df %>%
  arrange(desc(elpd_diff)) %>%
  select(fit, model_num, elpd, se_elpd, elpd_diff, se_diff, weight) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```


## Figure builder

```{r figure-builder}
# x_value = "delta"    -> ELPD difference vs. best model (loo_compare convention; the
#                          uncertainty that actually separates models). vline at 0.
#           "absolute" -> raw elpd_loo / elpd_kfold with its own SE. vline at the best.
#   cell_aspect = physical cell height / width; used to keep the colour fill SQUARE
#                 (horizontal border is widened relative to the vertical border).
#   v_border    = vertical border width as a fraction of one cell's width.
#   style       = "grid"  -> grey grid behind white/colour fills (default).
#                 "lines" -> grid hidden (white), thin black vertical rules between
#                            covariate columns. line_lwd sets the rule thickness.
make_comparison_figure <- function(g, title, criterion_lab,
                                   x_value = c("delta", "absolute"),
                                   cell_aspect = 1.2, v_border = 0.10,
                                   style = c("grid", "lines"), line_lwd = 0.3) {
  x_value <- match.arg(x_value)
  style   <- match.arg(style)
  df <- g$df
  n  <- nrow(df)

  if (x_value == "delta") {
    df <- df %>% mutate(xx = elpd_diff, xlo = elpd_diff - se_diff, xhi = elpd_diff + se_diff)
    xref <- 0; xlab <- expression(Delta * "ELPD  (vs. best model)")
  } else {
    df <- df %>% mutate(xx = elpd, xlo = elpd - se_elpd, xhi = elpd + se_elpd)
    xref <- max(df$elpd); xlab <- "ELPD"
  }

  base_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9.5),
          plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4))

  # VERTICAL ROW ALIGNMENT KNOB. All three panels must share this y padding so the
  # table rows stay centred on the forest's ELPD points. The discrete forest/weight
  # axes expand by `y_pad` (range becomes [1 - y_pad, n + y_pad]); the continuous
  # covariate axis is pinned to that SAME range explicitly (geom_tile would otherwise
  # train the scale on tile edges and drift). Change in one place only.
  y_pad   <- 0.6
  nrow_c  <- nlevels(df$ylab)

  ## ---- left: ELPD forest -----------------------------------------------------
  p_forest <- ggplot(df, aes(xx, ylab)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = xref, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = xlo, xmax = xhi), orientation = "y",
                   linewidth = 0.5, colour = COL_POINT) +
    geom_point(size = 1.7, colour = COL_POINT) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = y_pad)) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "Model #") +
    base_theme

  ## ---- middle: stacking-weight column (text only; angled header) ------------
  p_w <- ggplot(df, aes(x = 1, y = ylab)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(weight >= 0.005, sprintf("%.2f", weight), "0")),
              hjust = 0.5, size = 3) +
    scale_x_continuous(position = "top", breaks = 1, labels = "Stacking\n weight",
                       limits = c(0.5, 1.5), expand = expansion(0)) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = y_pad)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    base_theme +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x.top = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 9),
          panel.grid = element_blank())

  ## ---- right: covariate grid -------------------------------------------------
  # Borders are grey GAPS (in data units) between an inset coloured tile and an
  # oversized grey background tile. Oversizing the grey tile by the border width
  # makes the outer/edge borders identical to the interior ones (fixes the skinny
  # left/right edges). The fill is kept SQUARE by deriving the horizontal gap (gy)
  # from the vertical gap (gx) and the cell aspect:
  #   (1 - gx)*cell_w == (1 - gy)*cell_h   =>   gy = 1 - (1 - gx)/cell_aspect
  gx <- v_border                                          # vertical border (frac of cell width)
  gy <- max(0.02, min(0.92, 1 - (1 - gx) / cell_aspect))  # horizontal border (frac of cell height)

  cov_cols <- g$cov_cols
  cov_long <- df %>%
    select(ylab, all_of(cov_cols)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-ylab, names_to = "covariate", values_to = "present") %>%
    mutate(row_idx = as.integer(ylab),
           col_idx = as.integer(factor(covariate, levels = cov_cols)))

  # Background tile carries the grid colour in "grid" style; in "lines" style it is
  # white (invisible) so the grey grid disappears. Keeping the same oversized tile in
  # both styles preserves the cell geometry, so `cell_aspect` (and square fills) carry
  # over unchanged between the two versions.
  bg_fill <- if (style == "grid") COL_GRID else "white"

  p_cov <- ggplot(cov_long, aes(col_idx, row_idx)) +
    geom_tile(width = 1 + gx, height = 1 + gy, fill = bg_fill, colour = NA) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = present), width = 1 - gx, height = 1 - gy, colour = NA)

  if (style == "lines") {
    # thin black vertical rules bounding every covariate column
    vbreaks <- seq(0.5, length(cov_cols) + 0.5, by = 1)
    p_cov <- p_cov +
      annotate("segment", x = vbreaks, xend = vbreaks, y = 0.5, yend = nrow_c + 0.5,
               colour = "black", linewidth = line_lwd)
  }

  p_cov <- p_cov +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = FILL_COV, `FALSE` = FILL_EMPTY),
                      guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(cov_cols), labels = cov_cols,
                       position = "top", expand = expansion(0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1 - y_pad, nrow_c + y_pad),
                       expand = expansion(0), oob = scales::oob_keep) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    base_theme +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x.top = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 8),
          panel.grid = element_blank(),
          plot.margin = margin(4, 14, 4, 2))

  ncov <- length(g$cov_cols)
  p_forest + p_w + p_cov +
    plot_layout(widths = grid::unit(
      c(PANEL_FOREST_IN, PANEL_WEIGHT_IN, PANEL_CELL_IN * ncov), "in")) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = title,
      theme = theme(plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
                    plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 2, 4)))
}

# Open a vector PDF device that renders the Δ / × glyphs. Prefer the macOS quartz
# engine (always available here); fall back to cairo (Linux), then base pdf().
open_pdf_device <- function(path, w, h) {
  if (capabilities("aqua")) {
    grDevices::quartz(file = path, type = "pdf", width = w, height = h, bg = "white")
  } else if (capabilities("cairo")) {
    grDevices::cairo_pdf(filename = path, width = w, height = h, bg = "white")
  } else {
    grDevices::pdf(file = path, width = w, height = h, bg = "white", encoding = "ISOLatin1")
  }
}

# Save at a size that scales with the number of rows / covariate columns.
# Writes a vector PDF and a 300-dpi LZW TIFF (no PNG).
# `file` may carry any extension (e.g. ".png"); it is stripped and replaced.
save_figure <- function(fig, file, n_rows, n_cov, x_value) {
  # Width = panels (absolute) + fixed decoration, so forest & columns match across figures.
  w <- PANEL_FOREST_IN + PANEL_WEIGHT_IN + PANEL_CELL_IN * n_cov + PANEL_DECOR_IN
  h <- 1.9 + 0.30 * n_rows
  base <- file.path(OUT_DIR, tools::file_path_sans_ext(file))
  open_pdf_device(paste0(base, ".pdf"), w, h); print(fig); grDevices::dev.off()
  ggsave(paste0(base, ".tiff"), fig, width = w, height = h, dpi = 300, device = "tiff",
         bg = "white", limitsize = FALSE, compression = "lzw")
  message("wrote ", base, ".{pdf,tiff}  (", round(w, 1), " x ", round(h, 1), " in)")
}
```


## EDSM — K-fold

```{r fig-edsm, fig.width=10, fig.height=8.5}
fig_edsm <- make_comparison_figure(
  g_edsm, title = "EDSM catch model comparison",
  criterion_lab = "grouped K-fold CV on (1 | StationCode)",
  cell_aspect = 1.40)   # calibrated to the saved figure size (cell height/width)
fig_edsm
save_figure(fig_edsm, "model_comparison_edsm_kfold.png",
            n_rows = nrow(g_edsm$df), n_cov = length(g_edsm$cov_cols))
```

## Line-style variants (white fill, thin black column rules)

Same data and layout as above, but the grey grid is hidden (white) and the covariate
columns are separated by thin black vertical lines. The vertical cell border is shrunk
(`v_border = 0.06`) so the square fills sit close to the rules; `cell_aspect` is unchanged
(geometry is identical), so the fills stay square. Saved with a `_lines` suffix.

```{r fig-edsm-lines, fig.width=10, fig.height=8.5}
fig_edsm_lines <- make_comparison_figure(
  g_edsm, title = "EDSM catch model comparison",
  criterion_lab = "grouped K-fold CV on (1 | StationCode)",
  cell_aspect = 1.40, v_border = 0.06, style = "lines")
fig_edsm_lines
save_figure(fig_edsm_lines, "model_comparison_edsm_kfold_lines.png",
            n_rows = nrow(g_edsm$df), n_cov = length(g_edsm$cov_cols))
```
